vibe.intro: Wispr Bro can read the code names and file names that VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf show on screen, through Accessibility. It never opens your project folder or your files.

vibe.recognizeHint: When you say a variable or function name that is visible in your editor, it is written the way your code spells it, such as getUserById or user_id.
vibe.fileTagsHint: In the Cursor or Windsurf chat, saying "index dot ts" writes @index.ts when that file is open in a tab or shown in the file list.
vibe.fileTagsNeedsChat: Available after you add Cursor or Windsurf to your editors.
vibe.fileTagsNeedsSetup: Available after you set up code name recognition.

promise.title: Private by design

promise.noCloud: Speech recognition, cleanup, and History run locally. There is no account, telemetry, cloud dictation, or cloud cleanup.

promise.models: Download speech and cleanup models from Hugging Face (huggingface.co).
promise.updates: When update checks are on, look for app updates on GitHub (github.com).

locations.title: Where your data lives

retention.audioHint: Audio expires after 14 days by default. Removing audio keeps its dictated text until the text limit.

choices.title: Privacy choices
choices.contextHint: Read nearby text only while dictating to recognize names and spelling. Context is not saved or logged.
choices.updatesHint: Contact GitHub to check for a new version. No dictation or personal data is sent.
choices.learnHint: After a dictation is pasted, notice words you fix in that text box and suggest them in Dictionary. Only the corrected word is kept; the rest of the text is never saved or logged.

help.title: Help with setup
help.body: Each step takes a few seconds. You can go back at any time, and if you quit, setup picks up where you left off.
help.download: Wispr Bro sets up speech recognition on this Mac while you go through these steps. Anything you dictate before it is ready is kept and typed out once it is.

welcome.title: Talk, and your words appear
welcome.subtitle: Hold one key, speak, let go. Clean text lands wherever you are typing.
welcome.privacy: Your voice and your text never leave this computer. No account, no cloud, no tracking.

move.title: Move Wispr Bro to Applications
move.body: Wispr Bro is running from outside your Applications folder. Moving it there keeps updates and permissions working.
move.note: Wispr Bro reopens by itself after the move and continues setup.

mic.guidance: Wired and built-in microphones work best. Bluetooth headsets can drop out or sound muffled.
mic.question: Do the bars move when you talk?
mic.noHelp: Choose another microphone below, then talk again.

shortcut.title: Test your shortcut
shortcut.instruction: Press and hold the fn key (🌐) on your keyboard. The key below lights up while you hold it.
shortcut.fallbackInstruction: Press and hold Control and Option together. The keys below light up while you hold them.
shortcut.unboundInstruction: No dictation shortcut is set. Use Edit shortcut to choose one.
shortcut.worked: It works. The key lit up.
shortcut.question: Did the key light up?
shortcut.changeFailed: That change did not go through. Try again, or use System Settings.

tap.body: This usually means Accessibility is not on for Wispr Bro. Turn it on in System Settings, then come back and press Try again.

secure_input.choice: A password field or another app is blocking keys
secure_input.title: Another app is blocking key presses
secure_input.body: While a password field or some apps (password managers, Terminal's Secure Keyboard Entry) have focus, macOS hides key presses from every other app. Close or click away from it, then try again.
secure_input.active: Right now, another app is blocking key presses.
secure_input.inactive: Nothing is blocking key presses right now.

globe.choice: The 🌐 key opens emoji or switches the keyboard
globe.title: macOS gives the 🌐 key its own job
globe.body: Your Mac opens emoji, switches input source or starts Apple dictation when you press 🌐. Wispr Bro can set “Press 🌐 key to” to Do Nothing. Your choice is put back if you stop using fn for dictation.
globe.changed: 🌐 now does nothing on its own

no_fn.choice: My keyboard has no fn key
no_fn.title: Use Control and Option instead
no_fn.body: Some keyboards have no fn or 🌐 key. Hold Control and Option together to dictate instead. You can change this any time in Settings.

practice.title: Practice: write an email hands-free
practice.instruction: Press fn and Space together, then talk. You don't need to hold anything. Press fn again when you're done. Try: “Hi Sam, thanks for the notes. Can we meet on Thursday at ten?”
practice.instructionFallback: Press Control, Option and Space together, then talk. You don't need to hold anything. Press Control and Option again when you're done. Try: “Hi Sam, thanks for the notes. Can we meet on Thursday at ten?”
practice.instructionUnbound: No dictation shortcut is set, so this practice can't start. Skip it for now and set a shortcut in Settings.
practice.waiting: Waiting for you to start talking…
practice.listening: Listening… press fn when you're done.
practice.listening_fallback: Listening… press Control and Option when you're done.
practice.queuedNote: Your words are saved. They appear here as soon as setup finishes, and they are in History either way. We'll move on by ourselves in a moment.
practice.nothing: Nothing came through. Check that your microphone is on and try again.
practice.filled: That's your email. Add more, or continue.
